scope: Actual ordinary Plane; source bytes, f64 placement, matrix, viewport, DPR, samples, pen, plane size, selection and output encoding matched. Offscreen guard is the same real original Line in both ingresses.

adapters: PlaneRow and walk_plane retain production field layout and frame equations; the owning row collection and bounds-return type are local adapters. Initial bound size is the production default 100 scene units.
The common vector/plane GPU owner selects the actual vs_plane entry and 186 vertices per plane. Shared object, translation, line, clipping and ink visibility bindings retain production layout.
The only shader edit changes the whole-object integer output to the original Scene ID. No grid, arrow, visibility, depth, coverage or selection expression changes.
View Plane Size is per viewer and updates line uniform byte 76 without rewalking or reuploading source rows. Ordinary Plane and Clipping Plane remain separate display paths.
shader_provenance.composition: shared(ink_source(shader!(plane.wgsl))): expanded/minified entry, ink visibility, scene, clipping, normals, physical output.

matrix: DPR1/2 x MSAA1/4 x half-size50/100 x selected/unselected
scopeNotes: This native comparison matches the complete frame without tolerance or exclusions, using the actual production Plane shader and current course renderer on the same device/queue.
Generated covered (nonzero-width opaque blue lid), generated print (zero-width lid), and original retained historical covered source are distinct serialized fixtures.
Source Plane fields and loaded-source digest survive course import/archive. The selected GUID is the original Plane GUID.
Covered/print cases do not assert GPU owner picking, control-point editing, browser interactions, or all possible occlusion layouts.
The historical 5204-pixel difference is preserved; passing current original cases do not erase that failure.
Windows Job Object enforces two processors and the recorded commit limit; it cannot enforce a separate zero-swap quota.

guard.swapCapNote: Windows Job Objects have no separate per-job swap quota; zero swap is not enforced.
guard.output: Inherited stdout and stderr; redirect the runner to capture a log.
